provider_query: 对比 React 官方的 managing state 和 Vue 官方的 reactivity fundamentals
answer:
These chapters do not teach the same layer. React’s [Managing State](https://react.dev/learn/managing-state) is an architecture chapter (shape, ownership, updates). Vue’s [Reactivity Fundamentals](https://vuejs.org/guide/essentials/reactivity-fundamentals) is a mechanism chapter (how values become tracked).

1. **Scope.** React’s chapter is about organizing state as the app grows: visual states, structure, lifting, identity, reducers, and Context. Vue’s page is about declaring reactive data (`data`, `ref()`, `reactive()`), mutation, deep tracking, and DOM timing. [[1]](https://react.dev/learn/managing-state) [[2]](https://vuejs.org/guide/essentials/reactivity-fundamentals)

2. **Mental model.** React: do not command the UI; store a status and derive the view from it (`useState` + conditional render). Vue: mutate reactive fields (`this.count++` or `count.value++`); the system tracks reads and triggers updates. [[1]](https://react.dev/learn/managing-state) [[2]](https://vuejs.org/guide/essentials/reactivity-fundamentals)

3. **Update style.** React replaces state through a setter and re-runs the component from a snapshot. Vue intercepts get/set (Proxy / `.value`) so in-place nested changes are reactive by default. [[3]](https://react.dev/learn/state-as-a-snapshot) [[2]](https://vuejs.org/guide/essentials/reactivity-fundamentals) [[4]](https://coddy.tech/docs/react/react-vs-vue)

4. **Derived data.** React’s chapter says not to store redundant state (compute `fullName` during render). Vue’s closest built-in is `computed()`, which caches and re-runs only when tracked deps change—not covered as the main topic of Reactivity Fundamentals. [[1]](https://react.dev/learn/managing-state) [[5]](https://vuejs.org/api/reactivity-core.html)

5. **Sharing.** React: lift state to the closest common parent, then props; later Context + reducer to avoid prop drilling. Vue’s fundamentals page stays inside one instance; sharing is a different guide topic. [[1]](https://react.dev/learn/managing-state) [[2]](https://vuejs.org/guide/essentials/reactivity-fundamentals)

6. **Identity and reset.** React treats matching tree position as the same state, and `key` forces a reset. Vue’s page instead stresses that new properties must exist up front (Options `data`) and that assigned objects become proxies (`newObject === this.someObject` is false). [[1]](https://react.dev/learn/managing-state) [[2]](https://vuejs.org/guide/essentials/reactivity-fundamentals)

7. **Complex updates.** React extracts many handlers into a pure reducer + `dispatch`. Vue keeps logic as methods or setup functions that mutate refs/reactive objects; batching is “next tick,” not a reducer pattern. [[1]](https://react.dev/learn/managing-state) [[6]](https://react.dev/reference/react/useReducer) [[2]](https://vuejs.org/guide/essentials/reactivity-fundamentals)

8. **Granularity.** Independent write-ups: React re-runs the component and diffs the tree; Vue records dependencies and updates dependents. That is why React forbids silent mutation and Vue encourages it. [[7]](https://www.telerik.com/blogs/react-vue-developers-part-2-state-effects-why-react-re-renders-differently) [[4]](https://coddy.tech/docs/react/react-vs-vue)

**Sources:** [react.dev/learn/managing-state](https://react.dev/learn/managing-state), [state as a snapshot](https://react.dev/learn/state-as-a-snapshot), [useReducer](https://react.dev/reference/react/useReducer), [vuejs.org reactivity fundamentals](https://vuejs.org/guide/essentials/reactivity-fundamentals), [reactivity core API](https://vuejs.org/api/reactivity-core.html).
